text:
jamie: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-chooser tweak we started seeing more streaming stalls on long-tail requests. I pushed a quick dashboard (https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/stream/phase-breakdown) with token-phase breakdowns. Initial hypothesis: kernel selection now prefers fp16 kernels for seq > 512 which increases kernel-switch overhead mid-stream.

sanjay: saw the alert for stream-stall-ux-rate on prod early this morning. any numbers?

jamie: quick snapshot from the dashboard: p50 stream_chunk_phase_ms: decode=1.4ms, dispatch=2.8ms, kv_lookup=0.6ms, network=0.9ms. p95 dispatch for route=/chat/stream jumped from ~6ms -> ~22ms for requests with seq>1024. overall client ack latency p95 increased ~15ms on those flows.

maria: can you paste the prometheus queries you used? did kv_hit_ratio change too? if kv miss rate went up we'd see extra IO that looks like a kernel hiccup.

jamie: query I used:```
sum by(phase,route) (rate(stream_chunk_phase_ms_bucket[5m]))
```also a quick kv metric: `kv_hit_ratio{route="/chat/stream"}` — looks stable at 0.92, so not an obvious cache cold start.

leo: I repro'd locally with a small harness. When kernel selection flips mid-request we end up reinitializing a small kernel context which pauses dispatch for ~12-18ms. Batching heuristics also regress because the scheduler avoids mixing batch members across kernel variants, so effective batch size drops for mixed-length traffic.

sanjay: are these stalls visible on client vs server traces? want to know if it's purely server-side work or extra RTTs.

jamie: both. server shows a dispatch pause window (we've added `server_dispatch_pause_ms` gauge). client traces show `client_ack_ms` rising by ~12ms for affected chunks. network latency is unchanged. also instrumented `kernel_switch_count` which p95 increased 3.8x on that route.

perf-bot: perf-bot: regression check -> kernel_switch_count p95 increased 3.8x on /chat/stream between 1812260000 and 1812340000. Related alerts: stream-stall-ux-rate, stream-chunk-late.

maria: candidate fixes: 1) hysteresis for kernel selection so we don't flip mid-sequence, 2) prefer kernel variants compatible with current KV layout to avoid rebinds, 3) relax batching guard to allow mixed variants when cheap, 4) add an explicit `kernel_selection_cooldown`.

jamie: +1 on hysteresis and cooldown. also want dashboard panels per-route: token-level latency breakdown (decode/kv/dispatch/net) and a heatmap of kernel_switch_count by sequence_length. will add an annotation for the kernel-chooser deploy so we can correlate.

leo: quick patch idea: `min_seq_before_switch=128` and `kernel_selection_cooldown_ms=250`. ran local sims with mixed seq distribution: p95 dispatch reduced from 22ms -> 8ms, kernel_switch_count down ~70%.

sanjay: can you push that to staging and run the long-tail replay + streaming TPS test? make sure Dedicated and Hosted both tested because kernel variants differ.

jamie: rolling to staging in 30m. will tag the deploy in the grafana dashboard. @perf-bot please schedule a re-run of the regression check after deploy.

perf-bot: ack — scheduled regression check at 1812346800.

maria: if staging looks clean we'll roll canary to a small percent on prod and monitor `stream_chunk_phase_ms` histograms + client-side ack distributions. also add a per-route KPI card for token cost vs latency so product can see unit economics impact. :eyes:

jamie: thanks — logging the follow-ups in the runtime backlog (GH-rt/1423) and will paste the staging link when it's up.
